summary: Not doped in any measurable way. The G and 2D lines both soften with laser power (G -1.86 +- 0.12 cm-1, 2D -5.15 +- 0.13 cm-1 from 0.5 to 5 mW), and the I(2D)/I(G) ratio stays constant. The G-2D shift direction (slope 2.8) is far from the hole-doping line (slope 0.70) and closest to the uniaxial-strain line. Three sequential spectra cannot separate a real tensile strain from laser heating, which shifts the lines the same way. Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for absolute positions: it is the least perturbed and sits close to the strain-free, undoped reference. Use the 2 and 5 mW spectra only to track the power trend. The strain/doping relation itself does not apply at 532 nm, so no strain or carrier number is quoted.

observations.finding: Data quality is adequate; no spikes or saturation. Si line calibration is consistent across the series.
observations.evidence: rl_qc: no spikes in any file; Si line at 520.86 / 520.90 / 520.91 cm-1 (offset +0.16 / +0.20 / +0.21 from 520.7); SNR of strongest band 82 / 120 / 164; point spacing about 1 cm-1; data start at 450 cm-1. The Si offset changes by only 0.04 cm-1 across the series, so calibration drift cannot explain the graphene shifts.

observations.finding: G and 2D both soften monotonically with power. The G shift is consistent with linear-in-power; the 2D shift is front-loaded.
observations.evidence: rl_series (Si-corrected, fit errors only): G 1581.14 +- 0.10 / 1580.43 +- 0.08 / 1579.28 +- 0.06 cm-1; 2D 2669.32 +- 0.11 / 2666.23 +- 0.12 / 2664.17 +- 0.08 cm-1 at 0.5 / 2 / 5 mW. Shifts vs 0.5 mW: G -0.71 +- 0.13 (2 mW), -1.86 +- 0.12 (5 mW); 2D -3.09 +- 0.16 (2 mW), -5.15 +- 0.13 (5 mW). Linear-in-P prediction from the 5 mW point gives G -0.62 at 2 mW (observed -0.71, consistent) but 2D -1.72 at 2 mW (observed -3.09, about 8 sigma off fit errors). Step slopes: 4.4 for 0.5 to 2 mW, 1.8 for 2 to 5 mW.

observations.finding: Power-induced G-2D slope is 2.8, which argues against doping and is closest to uniaxial strain.
observations.evidence: Delta(2D)/Delta(G) = 5.15/1.86 = 2.77 +- 0.3 (propagated fit errors). Reference slopes: hole doping 0.70 (Lee 2012 e_H); uniaxial strain 2.2 (Lee 2012 e_T); uniaxial sensitivities -64 cm-1/% for 2D and -23.5 cm-1/% for G give 64/23.5 = 2.72; Calizo supported-graphene thermal coefficients give 0.034/0.016 = 2.1. The measured slope is 4 sigma away from doping and sits between the strain and thermal values, so the ratio alone does not separate heating from strain.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2012, Nat. Commun. 3, 1024, arXiv:1209.0234 (e_T slope 2.2, e_H slope 0.70, p.5); Mohiuddin et al. 2009 sensitivities quoted in Ferrari & Basko 2013, arXiv:1306.5856, p.20 Eq. S10; Calizo et al. 2007, arXiv:0708.1223, Table I

observations.finding: I(2D)/I(G) is constant within about 2 percent, so there is no detectable doping change across the series.
observations.evidence: Height ratio I2D/IG: 2.73 / 2.76 / 2.69 (0.5 / 2 / 5 mW). Area ratio: 5.35 / 5.14 / 5.14. Height errors are 1 to 2 percent, so the -1.5 percent change is at the noise level. Doping would lower I(2D)/I(G) strongly.

observations.finding: Both G and 2D broaden with power, and G stays in the stage-1 width range.
observations.evidence: FWHM(G) 13.37 / 14.48 / 15.62 cm-1 (+17 percent); FWHM(2D) 26.18 / 26.98 / 29.86 cm-1 (+14 percent). FWHM(G) about 14 cm-1 is the stage-1 value (Cancado 2011 Fig. 5c); much wider would indicate stage-2 defects. Phonon-lifetime broadening with temperature is one explanation; sub-spot strain variation would broaden the 2D line mainly.
observations.source: Cancado et al. 2011, arXiv:1105.0175, Fig. 5c; Neumann et al. 2015, arXiv:1406.7771, p.2

observations.finding: Zero-power extrapolation sits close to the strain-free reference point, but only qualitatively.
observations.evidence: Linear-in-power fit through the three points extrapolates to G 1581.3 and 2D 2669.3 cm-1 at zero power. Lee 2012 origin is G 1581.6 and 2D 2676.9 cm-1 at 514.5 nm. G does not disperse in stage 1, so the G offset is -0.3 cm-1, within the +-0.3 cm-1 calibration quoted by Lee (Methods). Converting the 2D origin to 532 nm with about 100 cm-1/eV dispersion gives about 2669 cm-1, a rough match to the measured 2669.3 (dispersion coefficient is approximate). The 2D curvature makes this extrapolation uncertain by about 1 cm-1.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2012, arXiv:1209.0234 (origin p.4; calibration Methods p.10); Ferrari & Basko 2013, arXiv:1306.5856, p.7 (dispersion about 2x D, about 100 cm-1/eV)

observations.finding: No D band above noise at 0.5 mW; the defect density is low.
observations.evidence: D-window (1290 to 1420 cm-1) max residual 57 at 1365 cm-1 vs residual SD 23 (under 3 sigma). Detection bound I(D)/I(G) at most about 0.09 (3 sigma / G height 753). Cancado relation (validity L_D >= 10 nm, 532 nm) gives L_D about 40 nm (+-5.6), i.e. point defects spaced at least about 40 nm apart. A residual of 325 at 1334 cm-1 vs SD 97 in the 5 mW spectrum is 3.3 sigma on a noisier baseline and was not fitted by rl_fit; it needs a higher-SNR check.
observations.source: Cancado et al. 2011, Nano Lett. 11, 3190, arXiv:1105.0175, Eqs. 3-6, p.4

observations.finding: Single-Lorentzian 2D line with FWHM 26 cm-1 supports monolayer, but the I(2D)/I(G) height ratio is below the textbook value.
observations.evidence: One 2D component, FWHM 26.2 cm-1 at 0.5 mW (turbostratic graphite about 50 cm-1, Ferrari 2006 p.3); relation gives monolayer, high confidence. Height I2D/IG 2.7, below the about 4 quoted for graphene at 514 nm, which is consistent with substrate interference on SiO2 (Yoon 2009: 370 percent change in I2D/IG for a 60 percent change in SiO2 thickness).
observations.source: Ferrari et al. 2006, PRL 97, 187401, arXiv:cond-mat/0606284, p.2-3; Yoon et al. 2009, PRB 80, 125422, arXiv:0908.4322, Fig. 2

observations.finding: Silicon substrate shows no detectable heating across the series.
observations.evidence: Si position shift +0.05 +- 0.03 cm-1 from 0.5 to 5 mW (raw 520.865 to 520.908 cm-1); a heated Si line would soften. This does not exclude local heating of the graphene, which is thermally coupled through a thin oxide. The Si temperature coefficient is not in the reference notes, so no temperature was computed from it.

properties.name: layers
properties.source: Ferrari et al. 2006, arXiv:cond-mat/0606284, p.2 (single sharp 2D component); confidence moderate-high because the height I2D/IG (2.7) is below the textbook value (substrate interference)

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: tensile-like (both G and 2D soften with power); magnitude at most about 0.08 percent uniaxial if the whole power trend were strain
properties.source: Mohiuddin 2009 sensitivities (G -23.5, 2D -64 cm-1/% uniaxial) as quoted by Lee 2012 Fig. 3 legend and Ferrari & Basko 2013 p.20; confounded with laser heating; absolute strain is not reported because the Lee relation does not apply at 532 nm

properties.name: doping_type
properties.value: none detectable (no change in I(2D)/I(G); G-2D slope 2.8 vs hole-doping 0.70)
properties.source: Lee 2012 arXiv:1209.0234 e_H slope 0.70; Das 2008 arXiv:0709.1174 for I(2D)/I(G) falling with doping

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: low (no D band above noise at 0.5 mW; L_D about 40 nm lower bound)
properties.source: Cancado 2011 arXiv:1105.0175 Eq. 4 (relation validity L_D >= 10 nm)

caveats: The three spectra were taken one after another at the same spot. The shifts could be reversible heating, a time-dependent change (drift, adsorbate or photo-doping), or an irreversible change. The three spectra cannot separate these. A repeat at 0.5 mW after the 5 mW spectrum would test reversibility.

The 2D power dependence is non-linear (step slopes 4.4 then 1.8), while the G shift is consistent with linear-in-power. With three points and fit-only errors, the non-linearity could be a fit systematic (2D line shape or baseline), a real saturation, or drift between acquisitions. Not resolved.

Si correction (-0.17 to -0.21 cm-1) is applied to the absolute positions. It changes all positions by almost the same amount and does not affect the shifts. Absolute positions carry the calibration uncertainty of about 0.3 cm-1 quoted by Lee 2012 (Methods p.10).

The Lee 2012 strain/doping relation is outside its validity (513 to 516 nm). Its origin and slopes were measured at 514.5 nm, and the 2D dispersion (about 100 cm-1/eV) was used only as a rough 532-nm conversion. The G-2D slope at 532 nm is not established.
Literature slopes disagree: 2.2 (Lee 2012 strain line) vs 2.72 (ratio of Mohiuddin uniaxial sensitivities). The measured 2.77 +- 0.3 sits closer to 2.72.

The Calizo thermal coefficients (-0.016 and -0.034 cm-1/K, supported graphene) would convert the 5 mW shift into about 116 K (G) and 151 K (2D) above 0.5 mW if the shift were entirely thermal. I did not compute absorbed power or spot size, so I cannot say whether that is physical. The notes say coefficients from one geometry do not transfer to another.
The D-band bound (I(D)/I(G) below about 0.09) rests on a rough residual-SD estimate. The 5 mW residual at 1334 cm-1 is marginal and unresolved.
Intensity ratios depend on SiO2 thickness and interference (Yoon 2009). I(2D)/I(G) is used only for its trend within the series, not as a layer or doping number.
questions_for_user: What was the order of acquisition and the time between spectra? If the 0.5 mW spectrum is re-measured at the end, does G return to about 1581.1 and 2D to about 2669.3? Reversibility separates heating or strain (reversible) from photo-doping or damage (irreversible). Why it matters: it is the single measurement that decides between the two readings.
What is the laser power at the sample (after objective and optics), the objective NA and spot size? Without absorbed power and spot size, a heating estimate cannot be made.
What is the SiO2 thickness and the substrate stack? The thickness controls the interference that changes I(2D)/I(G) and the apparent layer intensity ratio.
Was the flake annealed, gated, encapsulated or suspended? Annealing on SiO2 shifts G and 2D by about 25 cm-1 (Lee 2012), so the annealing history sets the doping baseline.

Is the 2D nonlinearity real? Repeat the power series with more points (e.g., 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5 mW) at the same spot, in both directions. Why it matters: it tells you whether a single strain/heating line describes the data.
What is the spectral resolution and the Si reference line position in your system? Compare with the Si line used here (520.9 cm-1).

limits: The strain/doping relation (Lee 2012) does not apply at 532 nm, so no absolute strain (%) or carrier density is reported. Only the G-2D slope and the zero-power comparison are used, and they are qualitative.

Three sequential spectra at one spot cannot separate tensile strain from laser heating, or heating from a time-dependent change. The G-2D slope (2.8) lies between the strain (2.2 to 2.7) and thermal (2.1) values and is not decisive.
No quantitative temperature rise: absorbed power, spot size and the Si temperature coefficient are not given in the reference notes or the data.
Hole vs electron doping cannot be determined at 532 nm from this data (the Lee 2012 doping direction is for hole doping at 514 nm only).
The 2D nonlinearity and the D-band bound are at the limit of three spectra and fit-only errors. No electron, hole or strain sign conclusion is drawn from them.
No irreversibility test, no polarization data, no second laser energy: these would be needed to settle the mechanism.
